Each agent action appends a hash-chained record whose next input is derived from the prior record's unpredictable ripple, so no two agents can share a trace without collision. Registering a second identity forces replaying the full chain, and every replay burns one distinct dune-seeded nonce per step. The attacker's cost is one verifiable computation per identity per epoch, growing linearly with history depth and impossible to duplicate.
